# System Activity (Audit Trail) — Event Type Definitions

> **Sentosa (sts-bnk)** | Version 1.1 | July 2026

---

## 1. Overview

**System Activity (Audit Trail)** is the second tab in the timeline panel on the Incident Detail screen. It shows every event with `isOperational = false` — i.e. events auto-generated by the system or produced by a user action on the workflow, **as opposed to** manual `[Ranger Log]` / `[MANUAL]` entries from a Ranger/Controller.

| Item | Detail |
|-----|----------|
| **Data source** | `incident.log[]` array in MongoDB — each entry is a `LogEntry` object |
| **Main render file** | `src/app/incidents/[...id]/page.tsx` — `getTimelineEvents()` function |
| **Log-writing API** | `src/app/api/incidents/[...id]/route.ts` — POST actions & PUT |
| **Tab split** | `isOperational=true` → **"Incident Log"** tab \| `isOperational=false` → **"System Activity"** tab |

---

## 2. Event Type Groups

**15 event types** in total (including 4 sub-variants of the `audit` type), organized into 5 business-logic groups.

---

### Group A — Incident Lifecycle

| Type Key | Display Title | Icon | Trigger / Action | Message Template | Actor | Color |
|----------|---------------|------|-----------------|-----------------|-------|-------|
| `creation` | Incident Created | 🛠 | Virtual — generated from `incident.dateTime` (not from `log[]`) | `Incident logged under ID {incidentId} (Case ID {caseId}). Title: "{title}"` | `incident.createdBy` | info — blue |
| `audit` → **Workflow Milestone** | Workflow Milestone | ⚙️ | First log entry (event #1) — created together with the Case | `Incident logged under ID {id} (Case ID {caseId}). Classification: {type} - {subType}.` | System | neutral — grey |
| `completed` | Ground Activities Completed | ✅ | Log entry containing `"marked ground activities completed"` *(reserved — no API action produces this string yet)* | *(reserved — future use)* | Controller | active — green |
| `closure` | Incident Closed & Endorsed | 🔒 | `POST /close` — Duty Manager approves closure | `Incident approved and closed by {actor} ({role}).[Closure remarks: {remarks}] Record is now read-only.` | Duty Manager | active — green |

| Type Key | Display Title | Icon | Trigger / Action | Message Template | Actor | Color |
|----------|---------------|------|-----------------|-----------------|-------|-------|
| `assignment` (First assign) | Responder Assigned | 👤 | `POST /assign` — `body.addResponder`, when status = `Live` | `Responder assigned: {name} — by {actor}. Status changed to Live (Assigned).` | Controller | high — dark orange |
| `assignment` (Add) | Responder Assigned | 👤 | `POST /assign` — `body.addResponder`, when status ≠ `Live` | `Responder added: {name} — assigned by {actor}.` | Controller | high — dark orange |
| `assignment` (Remove) | Responder Removed | 👤 | `POST /assign` — `body.removeResponder` | `Responder removed: {name} — unassigned by {actor}.` | Controller | high — dark orange |
| `assignment` (Bulk update) | Responder Assigned | 👤 | `POST /assign` — `body.assignedTo[]` | `Responder assignment updated to: {names} — by {actor}.` | Controller | high — dark orange |
| `acknowledgement` | Dispatch Acknowledged | 🔔 | `POST /acknowledge` — Responder action; Status: `Live` → `Live (Acknowledged)` | `Responder {names} acknowledged dispatch. Status changed to Live (Acknowledged).` | Responder (`assignedTo`) | high — dark orange |
| `onsite` | Arrived On-Site | 📍 | `POST /on-site` — Responder action; Status: `Acknowledged` → `On-Site` | `Responder {names} confirmed arrival on-site. Status changed to Live (On-Site).` | Responder (`assignedTo`) | active — green |

| Type Key | Display Title | Icon | Trigger / Action | Message Template | Actor | Color |
|----------|---------------|------|-----------------|-----------------|-------|-------|
| `audit` → **Workflow Milestone** | Workflow Milestone | ⚙️ | `POST /notify-complete`; Status → `Live (Pending Controller Review)` | `{actor} has notified completion of ground activities. Status changed to Live (Pending Controller Review) — awaiting Controller verification.` | Responder | neutral — grey |
| `audit` → **Workflow Milestone** | Workflow Milestone | ⚙️ | `POST /complete`; Status → `Live (Completed)` | `Incident locked by Controller {actor}. All ground activities verified. Status changed to Live (Completed).` | Controller | neutral — grey |
| `submission` | Closure Submitted | 📤 | `POST /submit-endorsement`; Status → `Pending Endorsement` | `Incident submitted for Duty Manager endorsement by {actor}.` | Controller | review — yellow |
| `return` | Incident Returned | ↩️ | `POST /return` — DM returns to Controller; Status → `Returned` | `Incident returned to Controller by {actor}. Reason: {returnRemarks}` | Duty Manager | high — dark orange |
| `incomplete` | Marked Incomplete | ⚠️ | `POST /return-to-responder`; Status → `Live (Incomplete)` | `Incident returned to Responder for further action by {actor}[. Reason: {remarks}]` | Controller / DM | critical — red |
| `reopen` | Incident Reopened | 🔓 | `POST /reopen` — System Admin only; Status → `Live` | `Incident reopened by System Administrator ({actor}). Status reset to Live.` | System Administrator | high — dark orange |

| `audit` → **Workflow Milestone** | Workflow Milestone | ⚙️ | `POST /link-duplicate` | **[Master]** `Duplicate report {incidentId} linked to this incident by {actor}.` **[Slave]** `Incident linked as duplicate of {masterId} by {actor}. Record closed.` | Controller | neutral — grey |

### Group D — Audit / Field Updates

> All share the `audit` type — distinguished by the content of the log description string (lowercase detection)

| Type Key | Display Title | Icon | Trigger / Action | Detection Pattern | Message Template | Actor | Color |
|----------|---------------|------|-----------------|------------------|-----------------|-------|-------|
| `audit` → **Incident Details Updated** | Incident Details Updated | ⚙️ | `POST /update-fields` or `PUT` ancillary fields | contains `"ancillary fields updated"` | `Ancillary fields updated by {actor}.` | Controller | neutral — grey |
| `audit` → **Media Presence Detected** | Media Presence Detected | ⚙️ | `PUT mediaInvolvement.mediaAtScene = true` | contains `"media presence detected"` | `Media presence detected at scene.` | Controller | neutral — grey |
| `audit` → **Communications Team Notified** | Communications Team Notified | ⚙️ | `POST /update-fields` or `PUT` — `mediaInvolvement.commsNotified = true` | contains `"sdc communications team notified"` | `SDC Communications Team notified regarding media presence.` | System | neutral — grey |
| `audit` → **Workflow Milestone** *(fallback)* | Workflow Milestone | ⚙️ | Any log entry that **doesn't match** any pattern above | *(no pattern — default)* | *(any string)* | varies | neutral — grey |

### Group E — Media, Broadcast & Data Deletion

| Type Key | Display Title | Icon | Trigger / Action | Message Template | Actor | Color |
|----------|---------------|------|-----------------|-----------------|-------|-------|
| `broadcast` | Broadcast Dispatched ({type}) | 📡 | Virtual — generated from `incident.relatedBroadcasts[]`. Closure broadcast is created on `POST /close` with status `PENDING` — awaiting Controller confirmation before actual dispatch | `Template: {templateUsed} \| Recipients: {recipients} \| Status: {status}` | Controller / System | review — yellow |
| `attachment` | Attachment Uploaded | 📎 | Virtual — generated from `incident.attachments[]` (file upload) | `File "{fileName}" ({sizeMB} MB) uploaded.` | `att.uploadedBy` | info — blue |

## 3. Event Classification Logic (`getTimelineEvents`)

The `getTimelineEvents()` function in `page.tsx` reads `incident.log[]` and classifies each entry based on the content of the `description` string (toLowerCase). **Priority order:**

| # | Detection condition (contains / startsWith) | Type | Title | isOperational |
|---|------------------------------------------|------|-------|:---:|
| 1 | `"responder assigned:"` / `"responder added:"` / `"responder assignment updated"` | `assignment` | Responder Assigned | false |
| 2 | `"responder removed:"` | `assignment` | Responder Removed | false |
| 3 | `"acknowledged dispatch"` | `acknowledgement` | Dispatch Acknowledged | false |
| 4 | `"confirmed arrival on-site"` | `onsite` | Arrived On-Site | false |
| 5 | `"marked ground activities completed"` | `completed` | Ground Activities Completed | false |
| 6 | `"approved and closed"` | `closure` | Incident Closed & Endorsed | false |
| 7 | `"submitted for duty manager endorsement"` / `"submitted for review"` / `"submitted for endorsement"` | `submission` | Closure Submitted | false |
| 8 | `"returned to controller"` | `return` | Incident Returned | false |
| 9 | `"reopened by"` | `reopen` | Incident Reopened | false |
| 10 | `"marked as incomplete"` | `incomplete` | Marked Incomplete | false |
| 11 | `"ancillary fields updated"` | `audit` | Incident Details Updated | false |
| 12 | `"media presence detected"` | `audit` | Media Presence Detected | false |
| 13 | `"sdc communications team notified"` | `audit` | Communications Team Notified | false |
| 14 | Starts with `"[Ranger Log]"` | `update` | Ranger Activity Update | **true** |
| 15 | Starts with `"[MANUAL]"` | `update` | Chronological Log Entry | **true** |
| 16 | `entry.deleted === true` | `deleted` | Log Entry Removed | false |
| — | *(fallback — no pattern matched)* | `audit` | Workflow Milestone | false |

**Besides `log[]`, there are 3 virtual event sources:**
- `incident.attachments[]` → each file produces 1 `attachment` event
- `incident.relatedBroadcasts[]` → each record produces 1 `broadcast` event
- `incident.dateTime` → 1 virtual `creation` event ("Incident Created") — **not** from `log[]`

## 5. Actor Snapshot — Freeze Policy for User Info

> Applies to **every** event type above that has an `Actor` field. This is a mandatory rule when redesigning the audit log DB schema, and is kept separate from the type-classification section above.

### 5.1 Principle

Every log entry must **freeze** the actor's information at the exact moment the action occurred — it must **not** be joined/rendered against the current data in the `Users` table at read time. An audit trail is historical evidence: its value lies in accurately reflecting "who did what, under what authority, at that point in time" — not the person's current status.

### 5.2 Why — a worked example

Log entry: **"Incident approved and closed by John (Duty Manager)."**

John is later demoted to Responder. If the system dynamically joins the current role into the narrative, the old log line would silently become:

> ❌ "Incident approved and closed by John (**Responder**)."

This is **semantically wrong**: it implies a Responder (lacking the required authority) approved the incident closure, when in fact John held Duty Manager authority at the time — a fully valid action. In this context, role isn't just a display label — it's **the authority that the action's validity rests on**.

The risk isn't limited to display: if any downstream logic (compliance checks, approval re-validation, audit reporting, etc.) queries the actor's **current** role to confirm "did the approver have sufficient authority," the conclusion will drift over time — a past approval that was perfectly valid could be incorrectly flagged as a violation simply because the person's role changed afterward.

### 5.3 Role Change vs. Name Change

These two cases have different impact and need different handling:

| Case | Impact on **Audit log (history)** | Impact on **Live logic** |
|---|---|---|
| **Role change** (e.g. DM → Responder) | Yes — if not frozen, the narrative changes meaning and misrepresents the validity of a past decision (see 5.2) | Not directly — role isn't used for identity matching |
| **Name change** (e.g. "Ranger John" → "Ranger Michael") | No — keeping the old name in the log is correct, since it's a historical narrative | **Yes, and more severe** — see 5.4 below |

### 5.4 The specific risk of renaming: the system uses name as identity

Currently `responderId` **is literally the display name string** (e.g. `"Ranger John"`), not a stable `userId` — and this string is used to match identity/permissions in several places, not just for display:

| File | Line | Purpose of the match |
|---|---|---|
| `src/app/incidents/[...id]/page.tsx` | 788 | `activeResponders.find(r => r.responderId === username)` — determines "is this me" to allow acknowledge/complete |
| `src/app/incidents/[...id]/page.tsx` | 2167 | `r.responderId === username` — shows "my" action buttons |
| `src/app/api/incidents/[...id]/route.ts` | 104, 267, 282, 302, 324, 345, 499 | Assign / remove / eligibility checks — matched via `responderId === targetId` |

Consequence: if a user is renamed while actively assigned to an **open** incident, the match string no longer lines up → that person **loses the ability to act on their own incident** (can't acknowledge/complete), even though they're still the same individual. This is a real operational bug, not just a display issue.

### 5.5 Proposed schema fields

| Field | Role | Frozen? |
|---|---|---|
| `actorId` | Stable FK to `Users.id` — used for **all** identity/permission matching logic | Does not change with name/role |
| `actorNameSnapshot` | Display name at the exact moment the log was written | Frozen permanently |
| `actorRoleSnapshot` | Role/authority at the exact moment the log was written | Frozen permanently |

Rule of application: all "is this the same person" matching logic (assignment, permissions, eligibility, etc.) should move to using `actorId`; `actorNameSnapshot` / `actorRoleSnapshot` exist purely to render the narrative text and must never be overwritten with live data from `Users`. If you need to know "who this person currently is / what role they currently hold," that's a separate UI lookup via `actorId` (e.g. a tooltip: "now Sarah Tan") — kept entirely separate from the original snapshot content.
